title: Unify GPU dependency contracts and add runtime instrumentation for safer upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Over time, divergent packaging and probe behavior across platforms has increased upgrade risk during CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS rollouts. Different nodes surface incompatible shared object versions or emit noisy symbol resolution failures that cascade into warmup jitter and rare cold-start crashes. This ticket consolidates the 'dependency contract' surface (what we promise to an in-tree and third-party kernel) and adds lightweight runtime instrumentation to detect contract drift during canaries and early rollouts.

Goals:
- Define a minimal, versioned GPU dependency contract document that runtime code and packaging tooling will consult during build and deploy.
- Implement a thin runtime contract verifier that runs during agent startup and emits structured telemetry for mismatches without blocking normal startup (fail-open by default).
- Add targeted instrumentation to capture probe timing, symbol resolution paths, and first-use kernel dispatch latencies to identify cold-path regressions.
- Provide a verification Canary job that runs on Dedicated pools to validate upgrades against the contract before broad rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- A machine-readable contract spec exists in the repo (contracts/gpu-deps-v1.json) and is referenced by packaging scripts.
- Startup verifier emits structured logs and metrics (contract.mismatch_count, probe.latency_ms.histogram, kernel.first_use_ms) visible in Console dashboards.
- Canary pipeline (ci/canary-gpu-upgrade) runs on a representative Dedicated pool and aborts rollout if mismatch_count > 0 or first_use_ms p95 regresses by > 30% compared to baseline.
- Documentation: Confluence doc explaining contract fields, upgrade flow, and incident runbook.

Non-goals:
- Full rewrite of the kernel loader or adoption of virtualized bundles (out of scope for this ticket).
- Blocking startup for minor mismatches (we will tune to fail-open initially).

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives from micro-version skew: mitigate via tolerance window in verifier and allowlist for known-safe symbol renames.
- Telemetry overhead: use sampling (1% by default) and aggregated histograms to limit cost.
- Canary false negatives: use low-volume canaries on Dedicated with synthetic warmup traces to increase chance of surfacing regressions.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge contract spec and verifier behind feature flag (runtime.feature.gpu_contract_verifier).
2) Deploy to internal integration fleet with enabled sampling and confirm metrics are stable for 72 hours.
3) Run canary pipeline on a small Dedicated pool for the new runtime-1.19 build.
4) If canary is clean, enable verifier for a staged rollout; increase sampling and remove fail-open for rollout stage.

Testing notes:
- Unit tests for contract parser and verifier (edge cases: missing SONAME, truncated symbol tables).
- End-to-end canary against nightly images with instrumented synthetic workloads (chat generation trace and KV cache reuse patterns).
- Benchmarks: measure probe latency and kernel-first-use across a matrix of GPU types (A100, H100) and image variants.

Deliverables:
- contracts/gpu-deps-v1.json (machine-readable contract)
- runtime/contract_verifier.{cpp,h}
- telemetry/metrics_mappings.yaml
- ci/canary-gpu-upgrade (pipeline job)
- Confluence: "GPU Dependency Contracts & Upgrade Flow"

Notes for reviewers:
- New verifier uses libc++ symbol iteration on Linux and a lightweight ELF header parse to avoid expensive full loads. We intentionally keep logic small and audited.
- Keep fail-open default; ops will toggle via Console feature flag when canary is healthy.
